mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates weakening labor market conditions, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances with positive RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls > 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 200k and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises > 10%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates reduced inflationary pressures, which can lead to a more accommodative monetary policy and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising real GDP (GDPC1) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 2% YoY and UNRATE falls > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.
